data.title: Japan, South Korea indices rise: Asian markets extend gains as AI stocks rebound
data.description:
Asian equities extended their rebound on Friday, November 27, as investors returned to artificial intelligence (AI) stocks after weeks of choppy trading.

The MSCI Asia Pacific index gained 0.6%, its second straight daily advance, with benchmarks in Japan moved higher, and South Korea opened higher before paring some of its gains.

In Tokyo, the Topix added 0.85% and the Nikkei 225 inched up 0.010%, while South Korea's Kospi gained 0.67%. Hang Seng futures fell 0.4%. Taiwan's TAIEX however, slipped 0.15% at open.

In Japan, Tokyo's consumer price index, excluding fresh food, rose 2.9% in November from a year earlier, the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications reported, the highest reading since July 2025. The measure which the Bank of Japan closely watches to understand underlying inflation, climbed 2.5%, while headline CPI rose 2.8%.

Tokyo's inflation number is significant since it often foreshadows national trends, indicating possibilities for a rate hike by the Japan's central bank next month.

Wall Street looked set to follow as futures on the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 each rose 0.7% ahead of a shortened US session after the Thanksgiving holiday. European shares also closed higher on Thursday, and that upbeat tone pushed copper up almost 2% from an 11-month low in London.

In India, the GIFT Nifty hinted towards a muted start in the red for the country's indices. Attention for the day's trade was particularly centered on the Nifty, which needed to close above 25,800 to secure a fifth successive weekly gain. The index last managed such a streak in June and July 2024, when it rose for eight weeks running.

US tariff plans add to the unease in the country after Washington proposed 25% duties on Indian imports on Wednesday, with a cap of 17% if the two countries agree a bilateral trade deal. According to experts cited by PTI, India's exporters could be at a disadvantage because the Section 301 excess-capacity probe covers only 14 trading partners and excludes rivals such as Pakistan, Sri Lanka, the Philippines and Turkiye.

In currency markets, the Japaneseyen held near 159.31 per dollar and the offshore yuan stayed close to 6.6610.

US Treasuries, meanwhile, fell as cash trading resumed, lifting the yield on the benchmark 10-year note two basis points to 4.87%.

Traders, however, seem to doubt the rally will last. Thursday's tech-led gains across Asia and Europe followed days of volatility driven by questions over the AI trade, and few catalysts appear ready to sustain the recovery. Investors now are likely to look to next month's US Federal Reserve meeting for hints on where borrowing costs are heading.

Oil prices meanwhile rose after Yemen's Houthi rebels attacked a major Saudi refinery. Brent crude climbed more than 2% to above $96 a barrel for January delivery, extending gains of over 6% across the previous two sessions, while West Texas Intermediate gained 1.5% to trade near $85.

Saudi Arabia's press agency, citing an unnamed Energy Ministry source, said the Iran-backed group struck the Jazan refinery on the Red Sea coast, halting some operations, killing one worker and injuring several others. The 400,000-barrel-a-day plant is the latest target in a run of regional attacks. The Houthis also claimed a strike on the 500,000-barrel-a-day Ras Tanura refinery, which Riyadh has not confirmed.

With Agency Inputs

data.title: AECOM to manage $15bn Adani infrastructure programmes in India
data.description:
Infrastructure consultancy AECOM has been hired to provide programme management for three multi-year Adani Group infrastructure schemes in India with a combined capital value of about $15bn, the company announced on November 23.

The appointment covers renewable power generation, electricity transmission and airport expansion. These sectors are central to the Indian government's Viksit Bharat plan to make the country a leading global economy by 2047. AECOM said the work would also help grow India's clean energy market and build up the infrastructure needed for long-term growth.

AECOM's role as Program Management Consultant covers the biggest of the three, the Khavda Renewable Energy Plant, a 30-gigawatt facility in Gujarat in western India that pairs battery energy storage systems with wind and solar power. The company said the programme ranks among the world's largest in renewable energy.

A second programme is set to deliver four transmission and substation projects spanning Gujarat and Maharashtra. These are intended to form a green energy corridor linking large renewable generation hubs with centres of high demand such as Mumbai. They are also meant to improve grid resilience and allow the network to absorb more renewable power.

The third assignment involves overseeing management, coordination and delivery across Adani's airport expansion in Ahmedabad, Mangaluru and Thiruvananthapuram. That programme aims to raise passenger capacity and improve regional connectivity.

'AECOM brings deep global expertise in program management across the energy and aviation sectors, underpinned by a strong local presence in India,' said Richard Whitehead, chief executive of AECOM's Europe & India region.

'We're proud to support Adani Group in delivering these ambitious energy and aviation infrastructure programs,' said Suvojoy Sengupta, chief executive of AECOM's business in India. 'Clean energy and improved connectivity will be critical to achieving India's Viksit Bharat vision, and we look forward to working closely with our client to help bring these transformative projects to life.'

data.title: Australia clears law requiring LNG exporters to keep 20% for domestic use
data.description:
Key points:
  • Policy will lower prices for families and businesses, PM says
  • Western Australia exempted from reservation scheme
  • Critics argue policy will discourage exploration, investment

By Renju Jose

Australia's Parliament on Friday passed the centre-left Labor government's gas reservation scheme, requiring liquefied natural gas (LNG) exporters to set aside up to 20% of their production for the domestic market from 2028.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the legislation would put "downward pressure" on energy prices for Australian households and businesses, although he did not specify the extent of any savings.

"Gas heats Australian homes, it firms renewable energy, it is essential to manufacturing ... and we will now have for the first time legislation preserving Australian gas for Australians," Albanese told reporters after the bill passed.

The legislation cleared the Senate late on Thursday after the opposition Liberal-National coalition pledged not to block the bill, following Labor's decision last week to exempt Western Australia from the scheme. The amended bill returned to the lower house on Friday and was approved.

Western Australia, which accounts for about two-thirds of Australia's LNG exports, already operates its own 15% gas reservation policy and is not connected to the east coast gas market, where demand is highest and supply is in decline.

TIGHT SUPPLY, HIGHER PRICES

Australia's east coast gas market has grappled with tight supply, higher prices and looming shortages over the past decade, as production from mature gas fields off Victoria, historically its main source of supply, has dropped.

Some east coast LNG producers have bought up domestic production to help meet export commitments.

Three LNG export projects on the east coast operated by Origin Energy , Shell and Santos will be affected by the gas reservation scheme. Those projects export LNG mainly to China, Japan, South Korea and Malaysia.

Critics argue the policy could lower prices enough to discourage exploration and investment in new gas resources.

The Business Council of Australia said the policy's success would ultimately depend on whether it supports investment, lowers energy costs and preserves Australia's reputation as a reliable trading partner.

"We will need to monitor the policy closely to ensure it delivers against these tests, and getting the implementation right will therefore be critical to avoiding unintended consequences," Chief Executive Bran Black said.

data.description: Jefferies has raised its earnings forecast for the MSCI India index by about 1%, citing Indian companies' resilient earnings. data.title: Bitcoin miners log longest block gap since July at 98 minutes
data.description:
Bitcoin is designed to produce a new block roughly every 10 minutes. On November 26, 2026, the network took 98 minutes and 19 seconds.

That gap between blocks 977,697 and 977,698 is the longest since July. Anyone waiting on a confirmation during that window waited a lot longer than usual.

Miners went more than an hour and a half without finding a valid block. Transactions in the queue were stuck for over 90 minutes during the gap.

The last time the network stalled this long was July 6, 2026. Block 956,953 arrived after a 112-minute, 26-second wait, so November's delay is the second longest of the year so far.

Galaxy Research ranks the November gap as the 69th longest since 2011. It is also the third delay of this size in 2026, according to the firm's analysis.

Alex Thorn, who heads Galaxy Research, flagged the event and where it falls in the historical record. His team's data puts gaps of this length at about once every 18,600 block intervals, or roughly once every four months.

The longest verified gap in Bitcoin's history lasted 141 minutes and 1 second, in October 2011. November's 98-minute pause is long, but well short of that record.

The 10-minute block time is an average. It works less like a train schedule and more like waiting for someone to roll a specific number on a die with trillions of sides.

Miners compete by guessing numbers until one of them produces a hash that meets the network's difficulty target. Every guess is independent, so the network has no memory of how long it has already been waiting.

This is known as a Poisson process. In everyday terms, each new minute has the same odds of producing a block as the one before, no matter how long the drought has run.

Bitcoin holds that average in place through difficulty adjustments every 2,016 blocks. If blocks have been coming too slowly, the puzzle gets easier, and if they have been arriving too fast, it gets harder.

A single long gap barely moves that calculation. It is one data point among thousands, so the difficulty does not swing in response to one slow stretch.

For most holders, a 98-minute gap went unnoticed. Coins stayed put, balances did not change, and the ledger's security was not affected.

The people who noticed were those trying to move money. Exchange deposits, merchant payments and transfers between wallets all sat unconfirmed until block 977,698 landed.

Fees behave oddly in this situation. During normal congestion, users can outbid each other to jump the queue, but a block drought removes that option entirely since there is no block space to bid on.

Galaxy Research's view is that gaps like this come from natural variance in mining rather than a malfunction. Nothing in the available data points to an outage, an attack or a problem with the chain itself.

The numbers argue for calm. If gaps of this length show up about once every four months, as Galaxy's data suggests, then three in a single year is roughly what the math would predict.

The more useful thing to watch is the trend in block times across a full difficulty period rather than any single outlier. A sustained slowdown across hundreds of blocks would say something about network conditions, while one 98-minute gap mostly says the dice landed badly for a while.

The 141-minute record from October 2011 has now stood for well over a decade.

data.title: Bangladesh loses half of Adani's Godda power supply
data.description:
Bangladesh will get only half the electricity it normally receives from Adani Power's 1,600-MW coal-fired Godda plant in India's Jharkhand state until December 18, after one of the plant's two units shut for annual maintenance, India Today reported on November 25.

The outage comes as Bangladesh relies more heavily on imported power during a wider energy shortage. The country also faces rising living costs, wage protests by garment workers and political uncertainty ahead of a promised return by ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina.

The 800-MW unit went offline at about midnight on November 25-26, while the second unit of the same size keeps running as usual. Adani Power described the shutdown as planned and part of its regular upkeep programme, The Business Standard reported. The work covers inspections, servicing and preventive maintenance meant to keep the unit reliable and avoid technical faults.

The Bangladesh Power Development Board approved the shutdown on October 26, according to bdnews24.com. The board signed a 25-year power purchase agreement with Adani Power in 2017 that obliges the plant to deliver 1,496 MW.

Bangladesh imported an average of 46mn units of electricity a day from India in the first half of November. That compares with 33.6mn units in October, even though domestic demand and generation fell as winter set in, bdnews24.com reported.

Unplanned outages have also hit the plant. On September 10, a fault in a boiler feed pump took Unit 2 off the grid, and Adani's supply to Bangladesh dropped to 691.44 MW, down from 1,430.06 MW during the September 9 evening peak. Three days passed before the unit was running again.

That month the power shortfall in Bangladesh hit 3,000-3,500 MW, leaving several districts without electricity for between three and 10 hours daily. In protest, an alliance of 11 parties headed by Jamaat-e-Islami undertook a long march that ran from Dhaka to Chattogram.

According to The Daily Star, the electricity prices Bangladesh charges retail customers went up 16.68% in June. Then, with import costs and global oil prices rising, the government increased what it charges for diesel, petrol and kerosene in September.

Hasina, now living in exile in India, will come back on December 16, according to one of her aides. Members of the Awami League who hid after the uprising are beginning to resurface. There have been reports of clashes involving police, as well as arson attacks targeting police stations, properties tied to the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, and the ancestral house of Muhammad Yunus, who heads the interim government.

data.title: Australia Orders LNG Exporters Reserve Some Gas to Plug Shortages at Home
data.description:
By Rhiannon Hoyle

Australia will require liquefied natural gas exporters to reserve up to a fifth of their shipments for the domestic market to help lower power bills for local households and businesses.

The law, approved early Friday, comes amid forecasts of supply shortfalls along the country's densely populated east coast--including Sydney and Melbourne--as traditional local gas fields deplete. The requirement takes effect Jan. 1, 2028, to align with industry contracting cycles, officials said.

"Australia has abundant gas resources and Australians should benefit from them," said Resources Minister Madeleine King. "This scheme will make more Australian gas available to our households and businesses, putting downward pressure on prices."

Australia is among the world's largest LNG exporters following significant investment by companies such as ConocoPhillips and Shell. The majority of Australian LNG is shipped to Japan, China, and South Korea, with about three-quarters sold under long-term contracts.

Write to Rhiannon Hoyle at rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com

data.title: Bank of America sees the S&P 500 climbing to 7,800 next year, making up lost ground
data.description:
The stock market will have to make up some ground in 2027, according to Bank of America.

Savita Subramanian, the firm's head of US equity strategy, expects the S&P 500 will climb to 7,800 by the end of next year. The target implies just an 8.3% climb from Tuesday's close that the strategist said represents a better entry point for investors after this month's corrective action.

It's also a level that the S&P 500 had already reached. The broader index first topped 7,800 in October, before a rapid succession of developments in November — including the exit and then reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO, and the Democratic sweep of Congress during the midterm elections — finally cracked a stock market that's been sputtering for roughly half a year.

The strategist expects that the choppy trading action could continue next year, as supply and demand dynamics deteriorate in the market and the question around AI sustainability continues to weigh on investors.

"What keeps us worried?" she wrote Tuesday. "Worsening supply (IPOs/issuance) vs. demand (waning buybacks, aging demographics suggesting risk of retirement fund outflows). Fading earnings/margin visibility and questions around the durability of the AI investment cycle plague us, and high expectations plus, until recently, S&P index complacency ('Don't risk it with single stocks, just buy the index') increase downside risk."

The conflicting cross currents in the market also implies a wide range of outcomes. The strategist expects that the S&P 500 can rise to 8,500 in her bull case, and fall to 6,600 in her bear case.

For the bulls, a neutral sentiment reading in the firm's sell side indicator implies double-digit equity returns. For the bears, a poor reading in the firm's earnings surprise indicator suggests earnings next year could disappoint investors, relative to expectations.

Still, there remain buying opportunities. The strategist highlighted communication services as a buying opportunity, raising the sector to overweight. She also expects AI adopters such as financials and health care will outperform.

One contrarian take she had was a switch to overweight consumer discretionary and underweight staples, thanks to an overdue housing turnover cycle that should mean a rise in discretionary spending as Americans make home purchases.

That could help investors wade through a bull market that's in its fifth year, with gains tougher to come by. Tuesday's trading was also volatile, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite dropping after rallying just the prior day. The broader index closed Tuesday just above 7,200.

data.title: Dollar lingers near 22-month peak as AI worries simmer
data.description:
The US dollar hovered below a 22-month peak in holiday-thinned trading on Friday, with traders looking to equity markets for clues on direction as doubts about the AI trade triggers heightened volatility.

The dollar index , which measures the currency against a basket of six peers, was steady at 103.81, at the end of a week that saw it pop to the highest level since March of last year at 104.53 on Monday only to erase those gains a day later. For the week, the index is currently flat.

The US currency edged up 0.1% to 159.355 yen early in Friday's Asian session, and also strengthened slightly to 0.83455 Swiss franc .

The euro was little changed at $1.0964 and sterling eased slightly to $1.3099.

The risk-sensitive Aussie dollar weakened a touch to $0.6631, after dipping to a one-year low of $0.6559 on Wednesday.

"All eyes are on whether the downtrend in AI-related stocks will turn around," Mizuho analysts wrote in a client note.

A recovery could see currencies such as the Aussie and high-yielding Mexican peso bounce back, while renewed selling would likely see those currencies under additional pressure, they said.

The US currency has been supported by expectations for Federal Reserve policy tightening with traders seeing a quarter-point interest rate hike on December 9 as a near certainty, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Hotter-than-expected US core personal consumption expenditures inflation in October, a sharp upward revision to third-quarter gross domestic product and a Federal Reserve survey showing continued economic growth and sticky inflation also have traders confident of an additional hike by around April.

The dollar index has risen about 5.7% so far in 2026, with only a month left in the year.

"The USD looks to be on a stronger-for-longer path than previously expected," NAB strategists wrote in a research report.

However, "given its rapid rise, we see limited scope for further gains," they added.

data.title: Young Thai Speaker Shares Family's Sustainability Story at UN COP31 with 51Talk
data.description:
Bodhi, son of 51Talk Thailand brand ambassador Shahkrit Yamnarm, shares his family's approach to sustainable farming at the UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Türkiye.

ANTALYA, Türki̇ye, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eight-year-old Bodhi from Thailand took the stage at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, to share how his family's durian farm inspired him to think about sustainability and climate change.

As one of nine young participants from six countries, Bodhi delivered a speech titled "A Tree for the Future." Through his family's everyday farming practices, he shared a personal perspective on how small actions can contribute to a more sustainable future.

Since 2019, 51Talk, a global 1-on-1 online English education platform, has helped young participants share their perspectives at UN events. COP31 marks the fifth time the brand has brought children to speak on a UN stage.

From a Family Durian Farm to the Global Stage

For Bodhi, speaking at COP31 was an opportunity to share a story close to his heart. In his speech, Bodhi introduced "2B2P" — Biomass Composting, Biodiversity, Pest Control, and Precision Irrigation — four ideas inspired by how his family cares for their durian farm.

He described how his family turns durian husks into compost to nourish the soil, grows different fruit trees to support biodiversity, manages pests while protecting beneficial insects, and uses water-efficient irrigation methods. Through these examples, Bodhi encouraged people to think about how everyday choices can help protect nature and conserve resources.

"I was a little nervous at first, but my dad told me that my voice matters, too. I wanted to tell everyone about our family farm and make my grandparents proud," Bodhi said.

Having taken English lessons with 51Talk for over a year, Bodhi prepared for COP31 through speaking practice supported by his teachers and family.

Beyond his speech, he also enjoyed meeting children from different countries and learning about their cultures.

"My favorite part was making new friends from different countries! We talked about our favorite things and learned about each other's cultures. It was so much fun that we could all speak English together," Bodhi added.

Building Speaking Confidence Beyond the Classroom51Talk helps children develop practical communication skills through personalized 1-on-1 online English lessons, structured curricula, and a global network of over 10,000 English teachers supported by professional training and teaching standards.

Through interactive lessons and individualized guidance, children have opportunities to practice speaking, express their opinions, and develop confidence in real-world communication.

Bodhi's COP31 experience demonstrates how English can help children share personal stories, connect across cultures, and participate in meaningful global conversations.

"Bodhi's experience at COP31 reflects what we hope more children in Thailand can achieve: the confidence to express themselves, connect with different cultures, and share their ideas with the world," said Emily Li, General Manager of 51Talk Thailand.

Global Communicator Curriculum Planned for Thailand in January 2027Building on its focus on practical communication, 51Talk plans to introduce Global Communicator, its new English curriculum, in Thailand in January 2027.

Based on a syllabus licensed by Oxford University Press and developed by 51Talk, Global Communicator features real-world, cross-cultural scenarios and immersive, task-based activities that encourage children to express opinions, solve problems, and communicate confidently.

AI-supported personalization and learning feedback help address individual learning needs and make progress more visible to families.

About 51TalkFounded in 2011, 51Talk is a global online 1-on-1 English education platform for children aged 3 to 15. Through interactive lessons, structured curricula, and personalized instruction, 51Talk helps young learners build practical communication skills and speaking confidence.

For more information, visit: https://th.51talk.com
